zh.title: 王曦 Xi Wang｜研究与数据分析作品集
zh.description: 王曦的个人研究与作品集：水同位素水文学、海洋食物网建模，以及金融、商业与产品数据分析。
zh.eyebrow: 地学研究 · 定量方法 · 实际问题
zh.name: 王曦
zh.role: 资源与环境硕士研究生
zh.intro: 关注水文与生态系统中的变化，也探索数据分析在金融、商业与产品决策中的应用。以统计学训练为起点，在地学研究中理解问题、检验模型、解释结果。
zh.heroAlt: Hi, I'm Xi Wang. 卡通地球、小熊猫与水獭一起阅读。
zh.rTitle: 水文与生态系统，两个研究方向。
zh.rIntro: 围绕降水稳定同位素和海洋食物网开展研究，重视观测与模型之间的联系，以及分析结果能支持怎样的解释。
zh.hydroTag: 当前研究 · 水同位素水文学
zh.hydroTitle: 降水同位素与天气背景
zh.hydroText: 整理降水稳定同位素、采样时间与气象资料，通过同一记录上的模型比较与不确定性分析，研究天气背景与同位素变化的关系。目前关注采样前天气能否在采样期间天气之外提供额外信息。
zh.ecoTag: 既往及延续工作 · 生态系统建模
zh.ecoText: 使用 Ecopath / Ecosim 研究功能群关系、营养通量与生态系统动态。工作涉及跨模型功能群映射、通量比较、敏感性分析，以及渔业和环境变化背景下的动态模拟。
zh.methodsText: 先明确对象与问题，再核对数据和指标；用可比较的模型与独立计算检查结果，最后把发现、解释和下一步验证分开。
zh.pTitle: 把定量方法带到实际决策中。
zh.pIntro: 两项已公开的分析案例，包含报告、数据、代码与交互工具。完整内容保留在案例页，首页展示问题与产出。
zh.etfTitle: 沪深300ETF产品比较与基金筛选
zh.etfText: 比较五只同指数产品在三个预设窗口中的费用、收益、风险与跟踪表现，将分析结果转化为筛选、并列比较和口径解释工具。
zh.etfAlt: 沪深300ETF筛选比较工具界面
zh.uniswapTitle: Uniswap单池活动、回访与集中度
zh.uniswapText: 从真实链上事件构建活动趋势、首次观察队列和集中度分析，讨论活动变化与头部贡献。结论限定为单池，地址作为参与者代理。
zh.eTitle: 从统计学走向地学研究。
zh.ynuDegree: 资源与环境 · 硕士研究生在读
zh.cTitle: 研究交流，也期待新的实践机会。
zh.cText: 关注数据分析、金融分析、商业分析与产品分析的远程实习，也欢迎围绕水文学、生态建模和定量方法交流。
zh.resumeNote: 可从简历中的链接查看完整项目。
zh.researchLead: 我关心自然系统如何变化，以及数据与模型能帮助我们理解其中的哪些部分。从研究问题出发，介绍数据处理、模型比较与生态解释。
zh.question: 研究问题
zh.hydroQuestion: 在考虑采样期间的天气、降水和季节之后，采样之前的天气是否还能增加雨水稳定同位素的信息？
hydroSteps: 核对水样的采样起止与时区，使同位素、降水与天气资料对应同一时间范围。
在同一批有效记录上比较基础模型与加入此前天气信息的模型。
用外部检验、分组比较及不确定性分析，检查增加的信息是否稳定。
zh.hydroFocus: 关注新增变量提供的信息及其稳定性；统计关系的解释同时考虑观测支持与物理背景。当前方向仍在推进。
zh.ecoQuestion: 不同海洋食物网模型中的功能群与营养流怎样进行可比较的整理？模型对生态系统变化的响应，如何受到结构与假设影响？
ecoSteps: 整理 Ecopath / Ecosim 模型的功能群、食性关系与营养通量。
对不同模型进行功能群映射与口径统一，比较营养流和消费者关系。
结合敏感性分析及动态模拟，讨论渔业与环境变化下的生态响应。
zh.ecoFocus: 关注跨模型比较的可解释性，以及模型结构、参数和情景设定如何影响结论。
zh.scopeText: 两个应用项目的报告、数据与代码可从首页进入。欢迎通过邮箱交流水文与生态建模的研究问题、方法和合作机会。

en.title: Xi Wang | Research & Analytics Portfolio
en.description: Research and applied analytics by Xi Wang: isotope hydrology, marine food-web modelling, and financial, business and product analysis.
en.eyebrow: Earth science · Quantitative methods · Applied questions
en.name: Xi Wang
en.role: Master’s student in Resources and Environment
en.intro: I study change in hydrological and ecological systems, and explore how data analysis can inform financial, business and product decisions. My training in statistics shapes how I frame questions, evaluate models and interpret evidence.
en.heroAlt: Hi, I'm Xi Wang. A cartoon Earth, red panda and river otter reading together.
en.rIntro: Two connected areas of work: precipitation stable isotopes and marine food webs. I focus on the relationship between observations, models and the interpretations they support.
en.hydroText: I align precipitation stable-isotope records with sampling intervals and meteorological data, and compare models on common records with uncertainty analysis. My current question is whether antecedent weather adds information beyond conditions during sampling.
en.ecoTitle: Marine food webs and trophic flows
en.ecoText: Using Ecopath / Ecosim to study functional-group relationships, trophic flows and ecosystem dynamics. The work covers cross-model group harmonisation, flow comparisons, sensitivity analysis and dynamic simulations under fisheries and environmental change.
en.methodsText: Define the question and population, check the data and metrics, then compare models and independently verify calculations. Keep findings, interpretations and the next validation step distinct.
en.pIntro: Two public case studies with reports, data, code and interactive tools. The case pages retain the full analysis; this page highlights the questions and deliverables.
en.etfText: Compare fees, returns, risk and tracking across five ETFs and three predefined windows. Translate the findings into a fund-screening and side-by-side comparison tool with clear metric definitions.
en.etfAlt: ETF screening and comparison tool; original interface in Chinese
en.uniswapTitle: Uniswap Activity, Address Return and Concentration
en.uniswapText: Build activity trends, first-observed cohorts and concentration measures from real on-chain events. Examine activity changes and leading-address contributions within a single pool, using addresses as participant proxies.
en.uniswapAlt: Uniswap activity trends; original chart in Chinese
en.ynuDegree: Master’s student in Resources and Environment
en.cTitle: Open to research exchange and new experience.
en.cText: Interested in remote internships in data, financial, business and product analysis. I also welcome conversations about hydrology, ecological modelling and quantitative methods.
en.resumeNote: Full project materials are linked in the CVs.
en.researchLead: I am interested in how natural systems change and which aspects data and models can help us understand. Explore the questions, data preparation, model comparisons and ecological interpretation behind my work.
en.question: Research question
en.hydroQuestion: After accounting for weather, rainfall and season during sampling, does antecedent weather add information about precipitation stable isotopes?
hydroSteps: Check sampling start and end times and time zones, aligning isotope observations with rainfall and weather over matching intervals.
Compare a baseline model and a model with antecedent weather on the same eligible records.
Use external evaluation, grouped comparisons and uncertainty analysis to assess the stability of any additional information.
en.hydroFocus: The focus is the information added by candidate variables and its stability, interpreted alongside observational support and physical context. This research direction is ongoing.
en.ecoQuestion: How can functional groups and trophic flows be made comparable across marine food-web models? How do model structure and assumptions affect simulated ecosystem responses?
ecoSteps: Organise functional groups, diet relationships and trophic flows from Ecopath / Ecosim models.
Harmonise groups and definitions across models to compare flows and consumer relationships.
Use sensitivity analysis and dynamic simulations to investigate responses to fisheries and environmental change.
en.ecoFocus: The focus is interpretable cross-model comparison and how model structure, parameters and scenario assumptions shape conclusions.
en.scopeText: Reports, data and code for the applied projects are linked from the homepage. Contact me to discuss research questions, methods and opportunities in hydrology and ecological modelling.
